findings.explanation: heading:hook ("A mortgage paid with a bill on a secret account") says the mortgage was paid. The section and Bryant (L16-L17, L34) say the opposite: the bank refused the bill, foreclosed, and the court held she "did not tender payment". s01 itself is accurate and is approved; the heading is held.
findings.suggestion: Say it was an attempt, e.g. "A mortgage she tried to pay with a bill on a secret account".

findings.explanation: "The strongest of it is Canadian" is true of the evidence as a whole (Netolitzky history, Canadian, 0.7, is the top verdict), but the study the sentence goes on to name (Netolitzky and Warman, 0.65) ties with the Australian source rather than being the strongest. Not wrong as worded; the editor may prefer "Much of it is Canadian".

The package limitation (one source's prosecutions concern tax filings, not debt instruments) is carried in substance: the callout says what the convictions are and that none shows an ordinary person paying a lender being charged, and s22 names the IRS as Heath's recipient. Buhtz (Bryant L34) is a bills-of-exchange conviction, so "can be prosecuted" stands for debt instruments.

The "absolutely no support" clause repeats the point of s33 in the court's other words; it is acceptable because the sentence's new point is linking the Treasury's own telling of the scheme (which starts at the gold standard) to that ruling, tying the two questions together rather than answering one again.
